sentences.text:
Sukhdev S/o Anop Gurjar, Resident of Bardiya (Nareda Road), Baran,
Police Station Kotwali Baran (Rajasthan) (At present confined in Distt. Jail, Baran) Versus The State
of Rajasthan Through Pp.

For Petitioner : Shri J.S. Chauhan
For State : Shri R.R. Gurjar, P.P.
 Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Sabina
 Judgment / Order
12/12/2017
Petitioner has faced trial in Criminal Case No.259/1996 pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Baran.

entities.text: Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Baran
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Trial court vide judgment/order dated 3.10.2001 ordered the conviction and sentence of the petitioner under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'Act').Appeal filed by the petitioner was dismissed by the Appellate Court vide order dated 7.4.2004.
Hence, the present petition by the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that as per the prosecution case petitioner was found in possession of adulterated milk.
Occurrence in the present case is of the year 1996.
Petitioner is facing criminal proceedings since the year 1996.

Learned counsel has submitted that he does not challenge the conviction of the petitioner as ordered by the courts below but has submitted that the sentence of the petitioner qua imprisonment be reduced to the period already undergone by him.
Petitioner is not a previous convict and is the sole bread earner of his family.

In support of his arguments, learned counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of this court in Loonaram Vs. The State of Rajasthan WLN (UC) 1977, 571 and on the judgments of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in the case of Bharat Lal Vs. The State of Haryana 1993(2) FAC Cases 65, Mahabir Parashad Vs. The State of Haryana 1993(2) FAC Cases 83 and Anil Kumar Vs. State of Haryana 2015(2) FAC 381.

In support of his arguments, learned counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of this court in Loonaram Vs. opennyai_summary.decision:

However,
sentence qua imprisonment of the petitioner is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
